tasks.short: Read the patient record and treatment plan, confer with therapists about the patient, note agreed changes in the record, and pass messages to therapists.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant reads the patient record and treatment plan
Physical therapist assistant confers with physical therapy staff to evaluate patient information for planning treatment
Physical therapist assistant notes agreed changes in the record
Physical therapist assistant passes messages to therapists on paper notes

tasks.design: The practice system ({OTHER}) shows the therapist's plan, goals and latest notes on one screen, and messages to therapists become tasks in the system instead of paper notes. Agreed changes go into structured fields of the treatment plan. Conferring with therapists stays with the assistant; changes to the plan are the therapist's responsibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were read across several notes and messages passed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems show plan summaries and hold tasks between staff.
tasks.still_hard: Therapists are in sessions and hard to reach between them.
tasks.human_edge: Telling the therapist what the patient said only to the assistant.

evidence.claim: Practice systems can show plan summaries and pass tasks between staff.
Notes enter the therapist's dossier, kept for 20 years, under the therapist's responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient file to the record updated; treatment decisions are the therapist's and outside.
Input contract: plans in the practice system; fallback is paper notes.

Conferring does not change. s1 keeps 70 because plan, goals and notes sit on one screen and reading stays; s4 keeps 60 because a task replaces delivering paper notes and the assistant still writes each message. A task to a therapist is the assistant's own save in the practice system.
Therapists read tasks between sessions as they read notes.
s3 is part of documenting progress notes, which sibling task 31-2021.00:21192 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: Do messages get lost less often?

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant closes finished tasks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small practice where notes were quick to hand over, so s1 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 80 (3.7); high: a rehabilitation centre with many staff (8.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct caregivers and family members on exercises and care, make home exercise programmes, answer their questions, and note the instruction in the record.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant instructs caregivers or family members on therapeutic activities
Physical therapist assistant makes home exercise programmes: sheets drawn or copied by hand today, assembled from the exercise library after the change
Physical therapist assistant checks the final programme: exercises, repetitions and cautions against the treatment plan, and the patient's app account
Physical therapist assistant shares the checked programme through the patient app
Physical therapist assistant answers family members' questions by phone
Physical therapist assistant notes the instruction given in the record

tasks.design: Home exercise programmes are assembled from an exercise library with short videos in the practice system ({OTHER}) so sheets are not drawn or copied by hand; the assistant checks each programme and shares it once through the patient app. Family members can watch the videos when they forget a step, which cuts some calls. Instructing in person stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercise sheets were drawn or copied and questions came by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Exercise libraries with videos are shared through patient apps.
tasks.still_hard: Older caregivers may not use apps.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a worried partner how to help without hurting.

reach.learn: Whether exercises are done correctly at home.

evidence.claim: Exercise libraries with videos can be shared with patients through apps.
Patient data shared through apps are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to the instruction noted; treatment changes are outside.
Input contract: exercise library licensed by the practice; fallback is paper sheets.
Caregivers watch videos in about the time they read a sheet; no added caregiver time.
Instructing in person, the programme check and sharing keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for choosing and adapting exercises; s3 keeps 80 because videos answer some questions.
s4 is part of documenting progress notes, which sibling task 31-2021.00:21192 covers; its saving is counted there, so s4 keeps its full time here.

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant helps caregivers open the app.

approvals.approved_version: The home exercise programme with exercises, repetitions and cautions exactly as checked by the assistant in s2b, shared once to this patient's app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many caregivers prefer paper, so sheets are still printed and calls stay; s2 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 100 (4.9); high: most caregivers use the app (13.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure range of joint motion and body parts, measure vital signs, and record the measurements in the patient record.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant measures patients' range of joint motion and body parts
Physical therapist assistant measures vital signs
Physical therapist assistant records measurements: on paper and typed into the record today; entered once on the tablet after the change, with blood pressure sent by the device

tasks.design: Measurements are entered once on a tablet in the measurement form of the practice system ({OTHER}), which charts them against earlier values to determine effects of treatments; connected blood pressure devices send their readings directly. Measuring stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements were written on paper and typed in later.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems have measurement forms with charts; devices connect by Bluetooth.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a patient guarding the joint during the measurement.

reach.learn: Whether trends are visible at review.

evidence.claim: Practice systems have measurement forms with charts, and some devices send readings by Bluetooth.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment session to measurements recorded; evaluation by the therapist is outside.
Input contract: measurement forms set by the practice; fallback is paper.
Measuring does not change. s3 keeps 45 because the paper copy and retyping go, and the assistant still enters each joint measurement once; blood pressure readings come from the device.

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant pairs devices with the tablet.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tablets are shared and many measurements are still written first, so s3 keeps 75 (5.7); high: entered once on the tablet as designed (13.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train patients in the use of braces, prostheses or supportive devices, give them instructions to take home, and note the training in the record.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant trains patients in the use of orthopedic braces, prostheses or supportive devices
Physical therapist assistant selects device instructions: copied sheets today, the supplier's instructions and videos for the device after the change
Physical therapist assistant checks the selected instructions match the patient's device and side, and the patient's app account
Physical therapist assistant shares the checked instructions through the patient app
Physical therapist assistant notes the training in the record

tasks.design: Device instructions and suppliers' videos are checked and shared once through the patient app from the practice system ({OTHER}) instead of copied sheets, and the training is noted with a short template. Training the patient stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were photocopied sheets and notes typed in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient apps can share instruction videos.
tasks.still_hard: Every patient learns the device at a different pace.
tasks.human_edge: Building a patient's trust in a new prosthesis.

evidence.claim: Patient apps can share instruction videos and documents.

assumptions: Boundary: from the device fitted to the training noted; device fitting is outside.
Input contract: instructions from device suppliers; fallback is paper sheets.
Training in person, the check and sharing keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because selecting from the library replaces copying sheets.
Patients open instructions in about the time they read a sheet; no added patient time.
s3 is part of documenting progress notes, which sibling task 31-2021.00:21192 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: Do patients call less with device questions?

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant adds supplier videos to the library.

approvals.approved_version: The device instructions and videos for this patient's device exactly as checked by the assistant in s2b, shared once to this patient's app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients want paper, so sheets are still copied and s2 keeps 80 (1.1); high: most patients use the app (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The physical therapist assistant keeps conferring, instructing, measuring and training patients; paper notes, copied sheets and retyped measurements shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the exercise library and measurement forms
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with more time with patients.
